thread.title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (GOOG, FB, AMZN, MSFT)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: The Earnings Beat: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (GOOG, FB, AMZN, MSFT)
text:
Shutterstock photo Will the market ever find some semblance of consistency? That’s the most pressing question these days -- despite stellar earnings from financial powerhouse Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and a surprise rebound in General Electric ( GE ) -- the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 200 points Friday.
The Dow’s decline was led by Apple ( AAPL ), which lost more than 4% Friday after Morgan Stanley issued a note warnings that the company's iPhone sales for its fiscal second quarter will disappoint Wall Street. Apple’s decline, combined with fears of rising interest rates, were too much to offset the start to earnings season.
Nevertheless, strong earnings results still did enough the push all three major indices higher for the week, lead by 0.6% rise in the Nasdaq composite Index. And with blockbuster tech earnings due out this coming week, there’s a strong chance that these gains — as I’ve been saying — are here to stay. In that vein, here are a few stocks to keep an eye on.
Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) - Reports after the close, Monday, April 23.
Wall Street expects Alphabet to earn $9.31 per share on revenue of $30.31 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $7.73 per share on revenue of $24.75 billion.
What to Watch: The top and bottom line numbers won’t be the only story here. There are a few changes in store for how the company reports its earnings. Earlier this month , Google said it plans to make adjustments to how it reports unrealized equity securities, how it measures ad metrics from third-party sites and how it reports revenue from its Nest unit
Facebook ( FB ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, April 25.
Wall Street expects Facebook to earn $1.36 per share on revenue of $11.41 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.04 per share on revenue of $8.03 billion.
What to Watch: Owing to negative headlines over user privacy and increased risks of U.S. government regulations, Facebook stock has suffered for most of 2018, down more than 5% year to date, while falling almost 15% from their 2018 highs at the beginning of February. Even so, Wall Street analysts remain broadly positive about the underlying health of the company, given that some 10% of ad spending in the U.S. this year is expected to go to Facebook.
As such, analysts have maintained a consensus Buy rating on FB stock, predicting the shares to rise nearly 30% to around $215. On Wednesday Wall Street will want some confirmation that this level of confidence, driven by a steady rise in revenue and earnings estimates, is merited.
Amazon ( AMZN ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, April 26.
Wall Street expects Amazon to earn $1.26 per share on revenue of $49.88 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.48 per share on revenue of $35.71 billion.
What to Watch: All eyes will be on (what else) the performance of Amazon’s Cloud platform AWS (Amazon Web Services), which has been and remains the company’s cash cow. Wall Street expects the AWS business to grow at around 40% year over year, which has been the average growth rate in the previous four quarters.
Beyond AWS and its top- and bottom-line results, analyst will want the company to weigh on accusations by President Trump that Amazon is not paying its fair share of taxes and it receives a sweetheart deal from the United States Postal Service.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, April 26.
Wall Street expects Microsoft to earn 85 cents per share on revenue of $25.77 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 70 cents per share on revenue of $23.56 billion.
What to Watch: Can the company’s Azure cloud must take the next step towards supplanting AWS cloud platform as the dominant solution? Evercore analyst Kirk Materne has been on record , saying Azure could grow at around 70% to 80% in fiscal year 2018, citing new features such as speech recognition and other tools. Assuming Microsoft’s slice of the cloud pie continues to grow to the extent Materne believes, MSFT stock — currently trading at around $94 — will finally crack the $100 threshold for the first time in its history.
